idiom_name: readonly record struct UserId(Guid Value) with a static Parse
implementation_notes: The wrapper is one declaration: a readonly record struct gets the single component, value equality, ToString and immutability from the compiler, so the hand-written IEquatable<T>/GetHashCode boilerplate disappears. Keep construction behind a private constructor plus a static Parse/TryParse (or validate in the primary constructor body) so the type cannot exist in an invalid state; a record class would add reference identity the pattern does not want, and a readonly struct is allocation-free. Serializers and ORMs see the single component, so add a JsonConverter or EF value converter where the type crosses a boundary.
pitfalls: A positional record struct makes the component a public property with an implicit constructor, so the raw value flows in unvalidated - declare the property yourself or keep the constructor private.
System.Text.Json/EF Core see one property: without a converter the value serializes as a nested object ({"Value":"..."}) and entity keys need an explicit value converter.
default(UserId) bypasses every constructor (structs always have a zero value), so a struct-backed newtype must tolerate or explicitly reject the zero/empty instance.

variants.name: StronglyTypedId source generator
variants.implementation_notes: Where the project already uses source generators and ids cross JSON/EF boundaries, the StronglyTypedId generator emits the wrapper (record or struct), its TypeConverter, System.Text.Json converter and EF Core value converter from an attribute - removing the per-type boundary code that otherwise makes the pattern expensive at scale. Choose it for libraries with many ids; hand-write the readonly record struct when you want no build-time dependency and a single-file type.
pitfalls: Generated types are build artifacts: editors, watch mode and CI see them only after the generator runs, and a stale generated file produces confusing compile errors.
The attribute fixes backing type and converters in source, so changing them later is a breaking change for every serialized payload and database column.
